issues.failure_explanation: On I^j, phi(t)=jh+delta^mu+(h-delta^mu)P(.), so phi is strictly increasing there only if h>delta^mu. Lemma (i) states strict monotonicity with no condition on mu; if delta^mu>h (small mu) phi decreases on I^j, and if h=delta^mu (the equality allowed by 'h >= delta^mu' in Theorem Inner-Lemma and actually used in the numerical tests) phi is constant on every I^j, so psi_q is not strictly increasing and psi_q' vanishes on whole intervals, contradicting Theorem Inner-Lemma's last claim.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis h>delta^mu (strict) to Lemma Shape-Lemma0(i) and Theorem Inner-Lemma, and note that h=delta^mu yields constant pieces.
issues.overall_effect: The strict-monotonicity claims of Lemma Shape-Lemma0(i) and Theorem Inner-Lemma are false outside h>delta^mu; the numerical section's parameter choice h=delta^mu produces staircase (piecewise-constant on intervals) inner functions, not the advertised strictly increasing ones.
issues.title: Strict monotonicity of phi asserted without the needed hypothesis h > delta^mu
issues.why_classification: A one-line hypothesis addition restores the lemma and theorem; no argument or rate is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: On I_q^{j}, psi_q increases by h-delta^mu, so Psi_q(C_q^j) is an interval of length |lambda|_1(h-delta^mu), whereas neighbouring images in the row direction are only lambda_p h apart. For Sprecher-like lambda (lambda_1 ~ lambda_2/(J+2)) with delta^mu << h (e.g. mu=2), moving x_2 within I_q^{j_2} changes Psi_q by up to lambda_2 h/2 ~ (J+2)/2 row spacings, so the argmin in (choosebox) returns a_q^{(j_1+k,j_2)} with k~J/2, whose center is O(1) away from x; g_q o Psi_q(x) then interpolates f at unrelated centers. For f=x_1 this gives per-level error ~1/(2N) at roughly half of the N levels, so ||f-f_N|| is O(1) regardless of J,N. The same happens for near-degenerate rationally independent lambda (lambda_1 ~ lambda_2 gives images a_q^{j+(k,-k)} within 2|lambda_1-lambda_2|kh of a_q^j). The step in (Nsquare2) that s_k=b_q^j with b_q^j the containing cube is thus unjustified; it holds only when |lambda|_1(h-delta^mu) is below half the minimal spacing of A_q (e.g. h=delta^mu, as used in the numerics, where psi_q is constant on intervals).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\bs{C}_q^{\bs i}$ be the closest hypercube determined by \eqref{choosebox}.
some neighbours of $(\bs A_{q}, \bs  B_{q})$ are not  neighbours of $(\bs c_{q}^{\bs j},   b_{q}^{\bs j}),$

issues.failure_explanation: For q not in Q the 'closest hypercube' is chosen by (choosebox), i.e. by |Psi_q(x)-a_q^j|, not by Euclidean distance. Even with staircase inner functions (h=delta^mu), when x lies in a gap in coordinate p>=2 at level q, Psi_q(x) sweeps from a_q^{i} to a_q^{i+e_p}, passing (for Sprecher-like lambda) through all of row i_p and the head of row i_p+1; the Psi-nearest image can be a_q^{(J-1,i_2)} whose center (1,c^{i_2}) is O(1) from x. Hence ||x-c_q^i|| <= sqrt(d)h/2 in (Oscf3) is unjustified, and each of the up-to-d gap levels can only be bounded by 2||f||_inf/N (as in the paper's own deleted draft). The total error is therefore O(h^alpha)+O(d||f||/N), so the refinement J=N^{1+gamma}, gamma>0, cannot improve the rate beyond O(1/N).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair preserving the stated rate identified; at minimum, replace the gap-level bound by 2||f||_inf/N per gap level, yielding ||f-f_N|| <= C h^alpha + 2d||f||_inf/N, and withdraw the gamma>0 improvement.
issues.overall_effect: The O(h^alpha)=O(J^{-alpha}) estimate (approximA), the abstract's O(N^{-alpha(1+gamma)}) claim and remark (approximAB0) are unsupported; at best an O(h^alpha + d||f||/N) bound is provable, independent of ISSUE-006.
issues.title: Gap-level error bound (Oscf3) conflates Psi_q-nearest hypercube with spatially nearest; gap levels contribute O(1/N), not O(h^alpha)
issues.why_classification: The advertised rate O(N^{-alpha(1+gamma)}) is lost; the surviving bound saturates at O(1/N) irrespective of J, a material worsening of the central guarantee.
